backlog.title: Restore spec compliance — fix the 8 TEST_RESULTS.md defects
backlog.description: Fix all 8 bugs reported in the TEST_RESULTS.md mini-PRD: 2 critical (BUG-001 inert config, BUG-002 stacked-rewind content reappearance), 1 major (BUG-003 checkpoint latest:user), 5 minor/cosmetic (BUG-004 branch scoping, BUG-005 silent persist failure, BUG-006 /reload, BUG-007 smoke SOFT coverage, BUG-008 audit suggestion). All fixes are surgical to the existing src/ modules; no new features. Baseline is GREEN (635 vitest tests pass). Every subtask implies write-failing-test → implement → pass (implicit TDD); code is not done without tests. Research findings live in plan/001_df2a6021905e/bugfix/001_8022a49f0aff/architecture/ (system_context.md, external_deps.md, design_decisions.md).

milestones.title: Configuration system wiring (BUG-001 critical + BUG-006 minor)
milestones.description: The entire configuration surface is inert (setConfig is dead code; getConfig always returns DEFAULT_CONFIG). Pi's ExtensionAPI exposes no settings accessor, so the only way to honor spec/09 §1 + README §3 is to read settings.json from disk. This milestone wires a new disk-reading+merge helper and calls setConfig at factory load AND on every session_start (which also fires on /reload — fixing BUG-006 in the same change). Outcome: every documented knob (enabled, thresholds, maxDepth, log.file, …) is honored, and mulligan.enabled=false makes all four tools refuse cleanly.

tasks.title: settingsLoader — pure disk-read + merge helper
tasks.description: A new Pi-free module that reads global ~/.pi/agent/settings.json and (when trusted) project-local <cwd>/.pi/settings.json, extracts the `mulligan` key, and applies project-local-over-global precedence. Never throws. Unit-testable with tmp-dir fixtures.

subtasks.title: Create src/settingsLoader.ts — loadMulliganSettings({cwd?, isTrusted?})
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (external_deps.md §1–§2) Pi's ExtensionAPI exposes NO settings accessor — verified by grep of types.d.ts. The ONLY way to honor spec/09 §1 is to read JSON files from disk. GLOBAL: path.join(os.homedir(), ".pi", "agent", "settings.json") (this machine HAS it; it carries top-level keys like "packages" — read ONLY the "mulligan" key, ignore the rest). LOCAL: path.join(cwd, ".pi", "settings.json"), read ONLY when isTrusted===true.
2. INPUT: opts: { cwd?: string; isTrusted?: boolean }. NO pi import (keep it pure/unit-testable). Use node:fs readFileSync, node:path join, node:os homedir — all already used elsewhere in this repo (markers.ts uses node:crypto).
3. LOGIC: loadMulliganSettings(opts) → read global file if present+valid-JSON → its `.mulligan`; read local file ONLY if opts.isTrusted===true (if present+valid-JSON) → its `.mulligan`; MERGE = local `.mulligan` REPLACES global `.mulligan` (top-level replace, NOT deep-merge — spec/09 §1 "project-local wins"). Return the merged `mulligan` value (type `unknown`) or `undefined` when neither contributes a mulligan key. NEVER throws: missing/unreadable file → skip; malformed JSON → console.warn(`[mulligan] settings: ${path} unreadable: ${msg}`) + skip; non-object `.mulligan` → return it as-is (let config.ts validateConfig coerce). No caching (the caller decides when to re-read).
4. OUTPUT: export `loadMulliganSettings` + its opts type, for consumption by P1.M1.T2.S1. When no mulligan key exists anywhere, MUST return undefined so that validateConfig(undefined) yields DEFAULT_CONFIG (verify).

subtasks.title: Unit tests test/settingsLoader.test.ts — merge, trust, never-throw
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: test convention is vitest with tmp-dir fixtures (mirror test/log.test.ts). settingsLoader is STATELESS (no module cache) so vi.resetModules() is not required. Write fixtures via node:fs + os.tmpdir().
2. INPUT: loadMulliganSettings from ../src/settingsLoader.js (built in P1.M1.T1.S1).
3. LOGIC: Assert each branch: (a) global-only file with a mulligan block → returns it; (b) local-only with isTrusted:true → returns it; (c) BOTH present, isTrusted:true → LOCAL mulligan WINS (assert the local value, NOT the global — this is the precedence regression guard); (d) isTrusted:false → local file is NOT read (returns global value even when a local file exists); (e) neither file present → undefined; (f) malformed JSON in global → warn emitted + falls through (undefined, or local value if local valid & trusted); (g) file present but no "mulligan" key → undefined; (h) never throws on any malformed input (wrap each case in expect-not-throw).
4. OUTPUT: a passing test/settingsLoader.test.ts that is the regression guard for the merge + trust-gate + never-throw contract. Pin ONE behavior for non-object .mulligan (S1 returns it as-is) and assert that.

tasks.title: Wire index.ts — setConfig at factory load + every session_start (fixes BUG-001 load + BUG-006 reload)
tasks.description: Call setConfig(loadMulliganSettings(...)) at factory time (global best-effort, no cwd yet) and inside the session_start handler (full read with ctx.cwd + ctx.isProjectTrusted()) for EVERY reason — session_start already fires on /reload, so this single wiring fixes both BUG-001 (never read) and BUG-006 (not re-read on reload). The existing resetRuntime call stays. The headline proof: mulligan.enabled=false in .pi/settings.json makes all four tools refuse.

subtasks.title: Wire factory + session_start handler to call setConfig
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (external_deps.md §3–§4) the factory signature `export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI): void` receives NO ctx, so project-local config (needs cwd) can ONLY be read inside an event handler. ExtensionContext exposes ctx.cwd (types.d.ts:217) and ctx.isProjectTrusted() (types.d.ts:234). SessionStartEvent.reason is "startup"|"reload"|"new"|"resume"|"fork" — re-read on ALL of them (cheapest correct; reload is a subset). config.ts setConfig(raw) already sets cachedConfig=validateConfig(raw) and getConfig() returns a clone.
2. INPUT: loadMulliganSettings from ./settingsLoader.js (P1.M1.T1.S1); setConfig from ./config.js (existing).
3. LOGIC: (a) At the TOP of the factory body (before setLogFile) wrap `try { setConfig(loadMulliganSettings({})); } catch { /* never break load */ }` — global-only best-effort. (b) In the existing `pi.on("session_start", (event, ctx) => {...})` handler, BEFORE resetRuntime, add `try { setConfig(loadMulliganSettings({ cwd: ctx.cwd, isTrusted: ctx.isProjectTrusted() })); } catch { /* never break session start */ }`. Keep the existing resetRuntime(ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()) call. Then re-call setLogFile(getConfig().log.file) AFTER setConfig so a reload picks up a changed log.file (log.file was read once at factory time; a reload may change it). Do NOT add async/await (factory stays synchronous per D8).
4. OUTPUT: index.ts now honors settings.json. Consumed by P1.M1.T2.S2 (integration proof). DOCS: README §3's "loaded lazily... re-read on /reload" and "Disabling" claims become TRUE — but the README text edit is Mode B (P1.M5.T1); here only verify behavior.

subtasks.title: Integration test — enabled=false disables all four tools (BUG-001 headline proof)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: test/index.test.ts already has createMockPi()/createMockCtx() helpers with vi.fn() and uses vi.resetModules() in beforeEach (config.ts caches cachedConfig at module scope — reset is REQUIRED so setConfig effects are observable per-test). The smoke harness note (jiti double-module) does NOT apply to unit/integration tests — same module instance.
2. INPUT: the wired index.ts factory + session_start handler from P1.M1.T2.S1; loadMulliganSettings; getConfig.
3. LOGIC: Write a test that (a) creates a tmp dir with `.pi/settings.json` containing `{"mulligan":{"enabled":false}}`; (b) builds a mock ctx whose cwd is the tmp dir and isProjectTrusted() returns true; (c) imports the factory, invokes it with a mock pi; (d) fires the session_start handler with the mock ctx; (e) asserts getConfig().enabled === false; (f) invokes one registered tool's execute (e.g. makeRewindTool's, or the handler captured in the mock) and asserts the result text starts with "Mulligan: refused — Mulligan is disabled". Add a second assertion that contextHandler returns undefined (pass-through) when enabled=false. Use vi.resetModules() + vi.mock or tmp files so settings are isolated per test; restore (delete the tmp settings) in afterEach.
4. OUTPUT: a deterministic test proving BUG-001 is fixed (the README §3 "Disabling" contract). This is the canonical regression guard for config wiring.

milestones.title: Filter targeting & protection correctness (BUG-002 critical + BUG-003 major)
milestones.description: The filter's live relative targeting (spec D7) is correct for a SINGLE rewind but breaks under composition: a second last_tool_call_group rewind re-targets the first (BUG-002 — originally-hidden content reappears, violating success criterion #4), and the latest:user protected role is never enforced for checkpoint rewinds (BUG-003 — a checkpoint rewind can delete the current ask). Fixes: pin each rewind's resolved target onto the marker at creation time and have the filter resolve against the pin; add the latest:user branch to protectedOk and a checkpoint pre-persist guard in the rewind tool.

tasks.title: Pin rewind targets at creation (BUG-002)
tasks.description: Add an optional hideEntryIds field (anticipated by existing TODO comments in markers.ts/transforms.ts). At rewind creation, map the resolved removal indices back to their source SessionEntry ids and store them on the marker. In the filter, when a rewind carries hideEntryIds, resolve its removal set by mapping those entry ids to CURRENT message indices (via a shared entry→message helper) instead of the live relative resolver — so a later rewind cannot retarget an earlier one and originally-hidden content cannot reappear. Markers without hideEntryIds fall back to live resolution (backward compat — the existing 635-test suite stays green).

subtasks.title: Data model — add hideEntryIds?: string[] to RewindMarker + RewindMarkerLike
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: markers.ts RewindMarker + RewindMarkerInput (Omit of envelope+id+seq+ts) and transforms.ts RewindMarkerLike both currently carry the comment "NO hideEntryIds — that's a later fix task" — the codebase ANTICIPATES this field. RewindMarkerInput is built in tools/rewind.ts (the payload object) — adding an optional field there is backward-compatible.
2. INPUT: the existing RewindMarker / RewindMarkerInput (markers.ts) and RewindMarkerLike (transforms.ts) interfaces.
3. LOGIC: Add `hideEntryIds?: string[]` to RewindMarker (markers.ts). Because RewindMarkerInput = Omit<RewindMarker, envelope+id+seq+ts>, it AUTOMATICALLY gains hideEntryIds?: string[] — verify TS agrees. Add `hideEntryIds?: string[]` to RewindMarkerLike (transforms.ts) and update its doc-comment to describe the field: "Optional pinned target — the SessionEntry ids this rewind resolved to hide at creation time. When present and non-empty, filterPipeline resolves the removal set from these ids (stable) instead of the live granularity resolver. Absent on legacy/unpinned markers → live resolution (backward compat)." Update/replace the stale "NO hideEntryIds" TODO comments. NO logic change in this subtask — types + docs only.
4. OUTPUT: the field exists on both interfaces; consumed by P1.M2.T1.S3 (capture) and P1.M2.T1.S4 (resolve). validateConfig/DEFAULT_CONFIG are untouched (hideEntryIds is marker data, not config).

subtasks.title: Extract mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices helper in transforms.ts (refactor resolveCheckpoint's walk)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: resolveCheckpoint (transforms.ts) already maps branch entries → message indices via `entryMessageYield` + a ctxEntries walk over `branchEntries` (filtered to context-producing types). That walk is the EXACT logic needed to map a set of entry ids → message indices. Extracting it into a shared pure helper avoids duplication and gives P1.M2.T1.S4 a clean seam. entryMessageYield returns 1 for message/custom_message/branch_summary and -1 for compaction/unknown (indeterminate).
2. INPUT: messages: MessageLike[], branchEntries: BranchEntry[] (root→leaf, passed to filterPipeline), entryIds: Set<string> | string[]. All from transforms.ts scope.
3. LOGIC: Add `mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices(messages, branchEntries, entryIds): number[]`. Build ctxEntries = branchEntries filtered to context-producing types (reuse isContextProducingType). Walk ctxEntries with a msgCursor (same as resolveCheckpoint step 4); for each entry whose id is in the entryIds set, compute its message-index range (msgCursor .. msgCursor+yield-1) and collect those indices; advance msgCursor by yield; if any entry yields <0 (compaction) OR msgCursor+yield > messages.length, return ONLY the indices collected so far for deterministically-mappable entries (skip the indeterminate one — never guess, never throw). Return ascending unique indices. REFACTOR resolveCheckpoint to use this helper for its target lookup where possible WITHOUT changing resolveCheckpoint's observable behavior (its existing tests in test/transforms.test.ts must stay green).
4. OUTPUT: a pure, unit-tested mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices, consumed by P1.M2.T1.S4. Add focused unit tests (test/transforms.test.ts): map a known entry id → its message index; compaction entry present → that id skipped; unknown id → not in result; empty entryIds → [].

subtasks.title: Capture hideEntryIds at rewind creation (tools/rewind.ts resolvePreview)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (external_deps.md §7 + design_decisions.md BUG-002 "Why pin by ENTRY id") resolvePreview (tools/rewind.ts) already builds a flat message list via `ctx.sessionManager.buildContextEntries().flatMap(sessionEntryToContextMessages)`. To pin consistently with the FILTER (which resolves from branchEntries via getBranch), build the index→entryId map from the SAME source the filter uses. CRITICAL COHERENCE: the pin captured here MUST be resolvable by mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices (P1.M2.T1.S2) using the branchEntries that filter.ts passes to filterPipeline (ctx.sessionManager.getBranch().slice().reverse()). Therefore build the preview message list + index→entryId map from getBranch() via sessionEntryToContextMessages (NOT buildContextEntries) so preview and filter share one entry source.
2. INPUT: ctx (ExtensionContext), the resolved `remove: number[]` index set (already computed in resolvePreview per granularity), P1.M2.T1.S1's hideEntryIds field on RewindMarkerInput.
3. LOGIC: In resolvePreview, while building messages, ALSO build `indexToEntryId: string[]` (for each yielded message, push the source SessionEntry.id). After `remove` is resolved, compute `hideEntryIds = remove.map(i => indexToEntryId[i]).filter((id): id is string => typeof id === "string" && id.length > 0)`. Return it alongside {ledger, k}. In rewindExecute step 7 (payload construction), set `hideEntryIds` on the RewindMarkerInput ONLY when the array is non-empty (omit otherwise → live fallback). NEVER let capture failure block the rewind: wrap in try/catch; on any error, omit hideEntryIds (the rewind still proceeds with live resolution — E13/E8). If getBranch() is unavailable on a minimal mock (some unit-test fakes), omit hideEntryIds (keeps existing tool tests green).
4. OUTPUT: new rewind markers carry hideEntryIds when the target is mappable; consumed by P1.M2.T1.S4. The existing resolvePreview callers (ledger/K) are unchanged. Add/extend test/tools/rewind.test.ts: a marker created against a fixture branch carries the expected entry ids on its persisted payload (assert via a spy on pi.appendEntry).

subtasks.title: Filter resolves against pinned hideEntryIds (transforms.ts filterPipeline)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (design_decisions.md BUG-002) filterPipeline (transforms.ts) currently re-resolves each rewind LIVE each iteration. The fix: when a rewind marker carries a non-empty hideEntryIds, compute `remove` from mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices(messages, branchEntries, hideEntryIds) instead of the granularity-specific live resolver. This makes each rewind's target STABLE — a later rewind cannot retarget an earlier one. protectedOk still gates every remove (spec/06 §8). Compaction: if a pinned entry is absent from the current branch (compaction removed it), mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices skips it → the rewind no-ops for that entry (correct — compaction already hid it).
2. INPUT: filterPipeline's existing args (messages, markers, config, branchEntries); RewindMarkerLike.hideEntryIds (P1.M2.T1.S1); mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices (P1.M2.T1.S2).
3. LOGIC: In the rewinds loop, read `const pinned = readOwn(rw, "hideEntryIds")`; if it's a non-empty array of strings, `remove = mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices(m, Array.isArray(branchEntries)?branchEntries:[], pinned)`; ELSE fall back to the existing per-granularity live resolution (partitionIntoUnits/resolveLastToolCallGroup | resolveLastTurn | resolveCheckpoint). Keep the `if (!protectedOk(m, remove, config)) continue;` gate and the `m = applyRewind(m, remove)` exactly as-is. Pure + never throws (E13). NO change to the shrinks loop.
4. OUTPUT: filterPipeline is pin-aware; backward compatible (markers without hideEntryIds behave exactly as before → the existing pipeline.test.ts composition cases stay green). Consumed by P1.M2.T1.S5 (regression test).

subtasks.title: Composition regression test — originally-hidden CONTENT stays hidden after a 2nd rewind
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (system_context.md + BUG-002 reproduction) the existing composition test (test/pipeline.test.ts ~line 252, "two rewinds with DISTINCT excludeToolCallIds") asserts ONLY role signatures and uses the spec §11 fixture where every group between rewinds is itself rewound — so it PASSES today despite the bug. The PRD's BUG-002 fixture has interspersed NON-rewound content (read→rewind→grep→rewind) where the originally-hidden read reappears. The fix's pin must keep it hidden.
2. INPUT: filterPipeline + mapEntryIdsToMessageIndices (P1.M2.T1.S4); the test's existing helpers (user/asst/result/custom/mkRewind/mkShrink, expectNoOrphans).
3. LOGIC: Add a test "two stacked last_tool_call_group rewinds with pinned targets keep originally-hidden content hidden (BUG-002)". Fixture messages (content-bearing, so absence is assertable): [user('u0'), asst(read:cRead), result(cRead,'BIG-READ-OUTPUT'), asst(rewind:cR1), result(cR1,'rewound'), custom('mulligan:note'), asst(grep:cGrep), result(cGrep,'GREP-OUTPUT'), asst(rewind:cR2), result(cR2,'rewound'), custom('mulligan:note')]. Markers (seq order): rewind#1 {seq:1, last_tool_call_group, hideEntryIds:[<entry id of the read toolGroup>]}, rewind#2 {seq:2, last_tool_call_group, hideEntryIds:[<entry id of the grep toolGroup>]}. Build branchEntries whose entry ids map to those toolGroups. Assert: JSON.stringify(out).includes('BIG-READ-OUTPUT') === false AND .includes('GREP-OUTPUT') === false (BOTH hidden), the two rewind assistant+result groups + both notes SURVIVE, and expectNoOrphans(out). Add a SECOND test asserting the SAME fixture WITHOUT hideEntryIds (legacy markers) still produces a valid (role-correct, orphan-free) output — documenting the live-fallback path.
4. OUTPUT: a content-level regression guard that FAILS on the pre-fix code and PASSES after P1.M2.T1.S4. This is the success-criterion-#4 proof.

tasks.title: Enforce latest:user protection (BUG-003)
tasks.description: protectedOk only enforces first:user; the latest:user selector is read from config but never acted on. For checkpoint granularity, resolveCheckpoint removes everything after the checkpoint target — which can include a user message that arrived after the checkpoint, crossing the latest:user boundary. Fix both layers (spec/06 §8 defense-in-depth): add the latest:user branch to protectedOk (filter), and extend the rewind tool's pre-persist guard to refuse a checkpoint rewind that would cross the latest user message.

subtasks.title: protectedOk — add latest:user branch + unit tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (transforms.ts protectedOk + spec/06 §8) protectedOk currently computes iFirstUser and checks min(remove) > iFirstUser. The latest:user selector is in config.rewind.protectedRoles (DEFAULT includes it) but never enforced. spec/06 §8: "a rewind that would remove the latest user message ... is refused". For last_turn default this is already protected by construction (resolveLastTurn only removes AFTER iLastUser, keeping iLastUser); the GAP is checkpoint (resolveCheckpoint removes everything after iTarget, which can be past a later user message).
2. INPUT: protectedOk(messages, remove, config) signature unchanged; ProtectedConfig.rewind.protectedRoles.
3. LOGIC: After the existing first:user block, add: if protectedRoles includes "latest:user", compute iLatestUser = index of the LAST role:"user" message; if iLatestUser !== -1 AND the remove set CONTAINS iLatestUser (any r === iLatestUser), return false (refuse). Fail-safe: malformed/missing config → enforce (mirror the first:user discipline: protectFirstUser defaults true; add protectLatestUser defaulting true when the roles array is absent/empty). NEVER throws. Empty/non-array remove → true (vacuous, unchanged).
4. OUTPUT: protectedOk refuses when remove would drop the latest user message. Add unit tests in test/pipeline.test.ts (protectedOk describe block): (a) checkpoint-style remove containing iLatestUser → false; (b) remove NOT containing iLatestUser → true; (c) config omitting latest:user → not enforced (true); (d) only one user message (iFirstUser===iLatestUser) and remove contains it → false (both selectors agree). Verify existing first:user tests stay green.

subtasks.title: rewind tool — checkpoint pre-persist guard refusing latest:user crossing + tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (tools/rewind.ts step-5b + design_decisions.md BUG-003) the existing step-5b guard refuses ONLY `last_turn && to_previous_prompt === true && k === 0` (nuclear across the first user message). checkpoint has NO equivalent guard. spec/06 §8 mandates the TOOL refuses before persisting (so no stray marker/note), with the filter double-checking via protectedOk (now added in P1.M2.T2.S1).
2. INPUT: rewindExecute's resolved `remove`/`k` from resolvePreview (already available at step 5); the messages snapshot; config.rewind.protectedRoles.
3. LOGIC: After step-5b, add a checkpoint-scoped protected check: if granularity === "checkpoint" AND protectedRoles includes "latest:user", compute iLatestUser on the resolvePreview message snapshot; if iLatestUser !== -1 AND remove includes iLatestUser, return refusal("would cross a protected message (checkpoint rewind would remove the latest user message — the current ask)", "checkpoint") BEFORE renderNote/persist. Mirror step-5b's shape (refuse + return, persist nothing). For last_turn default this is already construction-safe; do NOT add a redundant guard there.
4. OUTPUT: a checkpoint rewind that would hide the latest user message refuses at the tool and persists zero markers. Add test/tools/rewind.test.ts: fixture where a checkpoint's targetId precedes a LATER user message; assert the tool returns a "refused" text, pi.appendEntry is NOT called for a rewind marker, and pi.sendMessage (the note) is NOT called.

milestones.title: Branch scoping, persist integrity & audit polish (BUG-004 + BUG-005 + BUG-008)
milestones.description: Three independent minor/cosmetic fixes. BUG-004: marker/label reads use getEntries() (every branch) instead of getBranch() (current branch), so /tree navigation leaks sibling-branch markers. BUG-005: the rewind tool reports success even when appendRewindMarker failed to persist (null not checked). BUG-008: the audit Suggestion line hard-codes 'result'/'mulligan_shrink' even when the largest carrier is a user or assistant message. All three are small, isolated, and independently testable.

tasks.title: Scope marker/label reads to the current branch (BUG-004)
tasks.description: Switch getEntries() → getBranch() in the four marker/label reads: filter.ts readMarkers, tools/rewind.ts countRewindMarkers + checkpointExists, and the listCheckpoints call site in tools/audit.ts. getBranch() returns the current branch only; all four consumers are order-insensitive (bucketing/counting/latest-wins-via-getLabel candidate discovery), so no reordering is needed.

subtasks.title: Switch getEntries→getBranch in 4 sites + branch-isolation test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (external_deps.md §5 + design_decisions.md BUG-004) getEntries() returns EVERY branch; getBranch() returns the current branch root→leaf and is already used by contextHandler + resolveCheckpoint. The four leak sites: filter.ts readMarkers (~line 106), tools/rewind.ts countRewindMarkers (~207) + checkpointExists (~244), tools/audit.ts listCheckpoints CALL SITE (~563 — listCheckpoints itself is a pure fn taking entries[], so only its caller changes). All four are order-insensitive: readMarkers buckets by customType/kind; countRewindMarkers counts; checkpointExists discovers candidate targetIds then asks getLabel(id) for latest-wins; listCheckpoints builds its own latest-wins labelMap.
2. INPUT: ctx.sessionManager.getBranch() (returns BranchEntry[]/SessionEntry[] root→leaf).
3. LOGIC: In each of the four sites replace `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()` with `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()`. Keep the existing try/catch + defensive Array.isArray guards unchanged. For readMarkers, the bucketing loop is identical over either source. Do NOT change getBranch().slice().reverse() usages elsewhere (they are correct as-is).
4. OUTPUT: markers/labels from sibling branches no longer apply/count after /tree navigation. Add a test (test/filter.test.ts or a focused unit) with a mock sessionManager whose getBranch() returns ONLY branch-B entries while getEntries() returns A+B; assert readMarkers returns only branch-B rewinds/shrinks, and (for rewind) countRewindMarkers counts only branch-B markers. Verify the 635-test suite stays green (existing tests that mock getEntries may need their mock to ALSO provide getBranch returning the same array — update mocks minimally).

tasks.title: Null-check the marker persist result (BUG-005)
tasks.description: appendRewindMarker returns null when pi.appendEntry throws or getLeafId() returns null, but rewindExecute does not check — it proceeds to leaveNote and returns the success text. Add a null-check that returns a refusal and skips the note, so the agent is never told a rewind succeeded when nothing will be hidden.

subtasks.title: Add null-check refusal before leaveNote + test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: (tools/rewind.ts execute step 7 + markers.ts appendRewindMarker) step 7 is `const markerId = appendRewindMarker(pi, ctx, payload); leaveNote(pi, { content: rendered, rewindId: markerId ?? toolCallId });` — no null gate. appendRewindMarker returns string|null (null on appendEntry throw or null getLeafId). The shared refusal() helper prefixes "Mulligan: refused — ".
2. INPUT: markerId (string|null) from appendRewindMarker; the existing refusal() helper.
3. LOGIC: Immediately after `const markerId = appendRewindMarker(pi, ctx, payload);`, add `if (markerId === null) return refusal("failed to persist the rewind marker (nothing will be hidden); no changes were made", granularity);`. This MUST come BEFORE leaveNote so no stray note is sent for a failed rewind. details.markerId stays absent (it is only set on the success path). Keep the existing success path (leaveNote + successText) unchanged for the non-null case.
4. OUTPUT: a failed persist yields a refusal text and sends NO note. Add test/tools/rewind.test.ts: inject a fake pi whose appendEntry throws (and a second case whose sessionManager.getLeafId() returns null); assert the tool returns content text starting with "Mulligan: refused —", AND pi.sendMessage (the note) was NOT called, AND pi.appendEntry was attempted exactly once.

tasks.title: Audit Suggestion line — role-aware (BUG-008)
tasks.description: renderAuditReport always emits 'the `<rows[0].label>` result is the largest contributor. Consider mulligan_shrink.' even when rows[0] is a user message or an assistant message. Make the Suggestion honest per the largest carrier's role (shrink is meaningful for toolResult; rewind/shrink for assistant; nothing actionable for a user paste).

subtasks.title: Role-aware Suggestion line + per-role tests
subtasks.context_scope:
